title: Floss a dental training head's lower front teeth with a floss pick: ease it through, wipe both sides, bring it back out
instruction: Floss between the two lower front teeth of the dental training head with the floss pick: ease the floss through the contact with a gentle back-and-forth without snapping it into the gum, wipe each tooth's side up and down, then bring it back out.
context: Most adults floss, at least now and then (a third of US adults daily, CDC), by hand or with a floss pick, and parents and carers floss for others. Here a dental training head stands in for a person's mouth. The difficulty is placing and easing the floss: it has to land on the contact between two 5.4 mm-wide lower front teeth, a tight contact, while the pick's front arm slides down behind the soft lower lip. Then it is worked through with a light back-and-forth, stopped short of the gum, and pressed onto each tooth's hidden side down to the gum line. ADA: "Never snap the floss into the gums." Snapped onto the gum (a mark on a pressure film strip under the contact) or pressed into it, the floss scores 0. Stroked loosely in the middle of the gap, it cleans neither side: 0.25.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. Head: a fix-on-table dental training head (e.g. ANNWAH mouth simulator) stands upright, facing the robot, centred on y 0: a silicone face mask with soft lips over a metal head form, with no tongue, 152 wide and 170 deep, its crown 292 up. It holds a 28-tooth Kilgore/Nissin 200-type typodont (resin teeth screwed into soft urethane gums, as listed for D85SDP-200-GUB) in hinged jaws, the jaw at its open stop, 48 between the incisal edges. The mouth opening is 52 wide. The lower lip rests on the lower front teeth from their gum line up to 3 below their edges. The head's clamp grips the back edge of a 300 x 300 x 18 plywood board (x 235 to 535, y -150 to 150) standing in a taped outline on a digital shipping scale (300 x 300 platform, 40 high, 2 g steps); the scale's tethered display sits on the board's left front corner (x 245 to 290, y 90 to 140). Target: the contact between the two lower central incisors, at x 300, y 0, 140 up, 1.5 below their edges, the gum 2.5 below it; the incisors are 5.4 wide at the contact. Each incisor's facing side has four scribed marks framing a band 2 wide, centred under the contact, from the contact's lower edge to 1 above the gum line, and is sprayed green (Pascal Occlude occlusal marking spray). A strip of pressure-indicating film (Fujifilm Prescale MS, 0.4 wide, 6 long, about 0.1 thick) lies flat along the papilla's crest under the contact, held by a polyimide tape tab at each end on the gum, clear of the bands. Floss pick: a GUM Professional Clean Flosser, F-shaped (the floss runs parallel to the handle between two arms) with a ribbed control-grip handle: 75 long, floss 15 between the tips of two 10 arms tapering to their tips, handle 10 deep and 6 thick at the grip, plastic. It lies flat on the board's front right corner, handle along x, head away from the robot, arms to the robot's right, the handle's centre line at y -115 and its rear end 30 over the board's front edge. Phone: on a clamp tripod at x 300, y 350, 140 up, filming the mouth and the scale's display at 240 fps. Estimates: head size, mouth and jaw openings, lip position, contact and gum heights, tooth width, pick sizes. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Read every 50 ms step, the floss every 4 ms; in a real trial from the pressure film strip, the scale's display in a 240 fps phone video, and microscope photos of the two incisors taken out before and after the run. Wiped side: each band is read as a grid of 10 x 4 cells (0.2 mm columns between the scribed ticks, quarter-height rows between the grooves); a side is wiped when 32 of its 40 cells are bare, a cell counting as bare when bare resin covers at least three quarters of it on the after-photo (each tooth seated in its own putty jig under a Dino-Lite AM4113T at 50x, its 8 LEDs at a fixed setting, a 0.1 mm calibration slide for scale; sim: 4 points a cell, a cell wiped when the floss slid over 3 of them pressing that tooth). Passed: any cell in rows 2-4 of either band is bare. 0 for the rest of the run if: the film strip, checked unmarked before the run, shows a mark (marks only along the cut edges, narrower than 0.1 mm, from cutting, photographed before the trial, ignored); at any time, the scale under the board reads 300 g (3 N) or more above tare for 0.5 s; the floss pulls out of the pick or breaks; the head is moved 5 mm. Otherwise, from the final 1 s: 1.0: passed, both sides wiped, the floss back above the incisal edges; 0.75: passed, both wiped, the floss still between the teeth; 0.5: passed, one side wiped; 0.25: passed, neither wiped; 0: never passed.
reset_notes: Throw the pick away. Take off the face mask, lift the lower typodont jaw off the head's frame, unscrew the two lower central incisors from below, and screw in the next spare pair, each screw to its stop with the same screwdriver. Refit the jaw at its open stop, tape a fresh film strip, checked unmarked, on the papilla, refit the mask, re-tare the scale, and put a new pick on its mark: about 8 minutes. Spare pairs are prepared ahead: marks scribed, contact checked (a 0.05 mm feeler blade enters with resistance, a 0.10 mm one does not), sprayed (shake 10 s, 10 cm away, two 0.5 s passes, dry 60 s) and photographed in their jigs under the microscope. Re-spray any pair showing bare resin in the band.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX, 240 Hz. Teeth, gums, mask: static meshes. Incisors sit 0.3 mm back each (a 0.6 mm gap); task code holds the contact until the floss is pushed 8 N straight or 3 N sawing ±2 mm at 2 Hz, and from below until pulled up 3 N. Floss: a 0.5 mm task-code string at 5 N; only the robot's pick moves the string. Film strip: a mark at 2 N of floss on it. Lip: a sprung slide. A wipe needs ≥ 0.5 N of floss press. Head fixed; pick 5 g. Estimates: these forces. Demo reads object poses.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (3,600 steps; its right arm went to the mouth empty-handed and never picked up the floss pick); demo: 1.0
